The project objective is: Enhancing institutional and technical capacities for an effective implementation of the Enhanced Transparency Framework in Sao Tome and Principe.

The project will bring both socioeconomic and environmental benefits national and local levels by enhancing the national capacity to collect, analyse and share data that allows to monitor the implementation efficiency of mitigation and adaptation measures and to inform policymakers and the private sector. The improvement of methodologies for assessing, monitoring, and evaluating climate change related data across sectors, including social and economic impacts, will also inform broader policy areas and influence investment decisions. These efforts will contribute to the country’s sustainable development, advancing an integrated, climate-resilient, and low-carbon development pathway. Improved institutional frameworks, strengthened technical capacities, and comprehensive analyses will make climate action measures more effective and efficient. Furthermore, these advancements will enhance transparency in tracking and reporting support received and support needed, thus laying the ground for a closer and more effective dialogue with donors and climate finance actors. At the national level, the project will generate more robust and reliable information systems, with digital tools that will contribute to enhanced institutional ownership over information and to new opportunities for data sharing. The development of more consistent, comparable, complete, accurate, and transparent national GEE inventories will also contribute to improving the monitoring and evaluation of measures and sectoral objectives and support data-based decision-making. Progress in these areas will bolster transparency, deepen understanding, and facilitate the tracking and reporting of NDC objectives. Additionally, it will improve national statistical databases, including gender-sensitive information, providing valuable insights for inclusive and gender responsive policymaking. The new dynamic on data collection, analysis and reporting will bring new education and employment opportunities. By hiring 13 new junior contractual experts to work on transparency tasks within the national transparency system, the project will also contribute to retaining young graduates in the country and providing them with initial employment perspectives. In addition, to bring the voice of São Tomé and Príncipe to global and regional fora, the project will explore opportunities for meaningful participation in specific events where UNDP could support engagement with the global development discourse on reporting under the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) of the Paris Agreement and how enhanced reporting can feed into policy-making and a more effective implementation of the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC). The project will provide regional cooperation opportunities with countries implementing initiatives on reporting under the ETF in geopolitical, social and environmental contexts relevant to the proposed project in São Tomé and Príncipe. Under the Component 2 - Communication and training for broader ETF awareness and engagement, in “Output 2.1.2. - International and regional peer-to-peer exchanges are maintained to share lessons learned and good experiences in the management of national transparency arrangements and the preparation of reporting deliverables, incorporating gender perspectives.”, the project will deliver on enhanced South-South Cooperation by supporting a gender responsive participation of technical staff from key institutions of the national transparency system in peer-to-peer training and exchange events organized by global or regional networks, partnerships, or programs. It also contemplates the organisation of gender responsive exchanges between national and international transparency technical staff and experts to share lessons learned and good experiences, through visits to other countries that are part of the Paris Agreement or by hosting technical teams from other countries for an in-depth exchange of experiences on reporting under the ETF. The main target groups that will benefit directly from the project are:Ø The Coordinating Entity of the national transparency system, who will have a key role in ensuring a balanced and meaningful involvement of all relevant stakeholders in the national transparency system. Ø The members of the different Working Groups and organisations involved in the national transparency system as identified in the relevant institutional arrangements’ legal and regulatory framework. Ø The National Committee for Climate Change (NCCC) members.Ø Representatives from sectors involved in climate change policies and in the implementation of the NDC. Ø The private sector, civil society organisations and the academia. Ultimately, a broader set of stakeholders will benefit indirectly from the increased quantity and quality of available climate data across the different sectors. This will have socioeconomic benefits and people and companies will be able to take more informed decisions in a context where climate change impacts increasingly affect everyone, everywhere, especially those in more vulnerable situations, like women, children and youth and elderly people. A more detailed overview and analysis of the relevant stakeholders and respective engagement plan is presented in Annex 8 of the Prodoc.
